memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “Every word of God is pure; He is a shield to those who put their trust in Him.” — Proverbs 30:5

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
The scribes who wrote the Scriptures were not ordinary writers. They were men who dedicated their entire lives as a sacrifice and a cost paid to write the powerful words of God. They followed extremely strict rules while copying the Scriptures. Every letter, every word, and every line was carefully counted.
Before writing the Name of God, they purified themselves with holy fear. If even a single letter was written incorrectly, the entire scroll was rejected. They never attempted to correct it; instead, they rewrote the whole scroll afresh. Their writings were 99% accurate.
The remaining 1% was not human error, but prophetic portions meant to be fulfilled in the generations to come. What was written by men in faith, God fulfilled in His perfect time with absolute precision. That is why the ancient Scriptures are still revered today with deep reverence and godly fear.
The Scriptures were never altered for personal preference or convenience. Instead, they were preserved through suffering, patience, obedience, and the fear of the Lord. “Every word of God is pure.”
Let us remember our forefathers who lived holy lives to understand God’s heart, wrote His words as sacred Scripture, preserved the scrolls, and copied them with utmost care and precision. Their intense labor shines today in our hands as the Holy Bible.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “The Bible is not a product of human intellect; it is divine revelation, carefully preserved.” — R. C. Sproul

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, grant us holy fear and reverence for Your Word. Teach us to live truthfully according to the Scriptures written with sacrifice. Help us not only to hear Your Word, but to live by it.
In Jesus’ Name, Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: The Bible you hold in your hands was written with tears, discipline, and the fear of God. Do not handle it casually. Give it the honor it deserves. Let those sacred words speak to you.
